resourceProfile.assessment: The complete English and French source scope, prior review metadata, glossary, and project concept references were available locally.

automatedQuality.summary: Translation review metadata, queue validation, typecheck, 79 test files with 462 tests, complete build, 39 IIS rules with 61 route cases, and 724 generated-link checks passed.

linguisticCritique.summary: A bounded French pass identified 25 actionable circuit, technical-grammar, thermal, SI-conversion, and wire-gauge defects; all 25 were corrected.

competentHumanReview.summary: No competent French human review was performed in this cycle; changed IDs remain machine-drafted.

publicationAuthorization.summary: No merge, publication, deployment, or residual-risk authorization was requested or granted.

findings.summary: The Kirchhoff description was vague about the conserved quantities.
evidence: The previous text referred generally to conservation at nodes and around loops.
findings.resolution: Named charge conservation at nodes and energy conservation in closed loops.

findings.summary: The resistor relationship used less precise wording for voltage and current.
evidence: The previous bullet said to relate a resistor's voltage and current with V = I × R.
findings.resolution: Rewrote it as voltage across a resistor related to its current.

findings.summary: The TCR description said estimates rather than describes the resistance change.
evidence: The previous description used estime la façon for the definition.
findings.resolution: Changed it to describe how a material's resistance varies with temperature.

findings.summary: The SOH-CAH-TOA explanation used incorrect French ratio wording.
evidence: The previous text said sinus is opposite above hypotenuse and used an awkward adjacent construction.
findings.resolution: Rewrote the paragraph with the standard French ratio definitions.

findings.summary: The angle-mode paragraph used singular radian and an awkward full-cycle phrase.
evidence: The previous paragraph said une valeur en radian and Un cycle complet fait.
findings.resolution: Rewrote it with radians and a complete-turn formulation.

findings.summary: The network description omitted en before the series and parallel terms.
evidence: The previous text used réseaux série et parallèle.
findings.resolution: Changed it to réseaux en série et en parallèle.

findings.summary: The rearranged-formula instruction used rechercher instead of the natural technical verb trouver.
evidence: The previous sentence said the value to rechercher.
findings.resolution: Changed it to the value you souhaitez trouver.

findings.summary: The safety instruction used gérer for components handling current and power.
evidence: The previous paragraph said components can gérer the expected current and power.
findings.resolution: Changed it to support the expected current and power and retained the safety margin.

findings.summary: The heat-flux display name omitted the per-area density meaning.
evidence: The previous display name was Flux de chaleur despite W/m² content.
findings.resolution: Changed it to Densité de flux thermique.

findings.summary: The heat-flux description did not explicitly define transfer per unit area.
evidence: The previous description said heat crosses a surface without defining the density.
findings.resolution: Rewrote it as heat-transfer rate per unit area.

findings.summary: The heat-flux example title omitted the density term and used chauffage ambiguously.
evidence: The previous title was Flux de chauffage moyen.
findings.resolution: Changed it to Densité de flux thermique moyenne de l'élément chauffant.

findings.summary: The heat-flux conclusion named flux thermique while reporting density units.
evidence: The W/m² and W/cm² units represent density rather than total heat flow.
findings.resolution: Changed it to densité de flux thermique and retained both units.

findings.summary: The conduction bullet said flux from a temperature rather than heat transfer between temperatures.
evidence: The previous wording was unidiomatic: un flux d'une température.
findings.resolution: Rewrote it as heat transferring from higher to lower temperature.

findings.summary: The convection paragraph called h a surface coefficient.
evidence: The previous paragraph used coefficient de surface h.
findings.resolution: Changed it to coefficient de convection h.

findings.summary: The practical check used flux thermique instead of density of heat flux.
evidence: The bullet compared an average density with a local peak but named only flux.
findings.resolution: Changed it to densité de flux thermique moyenne.

findings.summary: The final practical check named flux thermique while describing a per-area transfer rate.
evidence: The check concerns q'' and W/m², so density is required.
findings.resolution: Changed it to densité de flux thermique and made the temperature calculation explicit.

findings.summary: The SI heading said common units rather than base units.
evidence: The heading did not distinguish the base-unit table from derived-unit bullets.
findings.resolution: Changed it to Unités de base du SI.

findings.summary: The decimal-prefix table contained a malformed mega symbol and spaced exponent notation.
evidence: The table used M. and 10 ^ 3/10 ^ 6 instead of SI symbols and notation.
findings.resolution: Restored M, μ, and compact powers of ten for all decimal prefixes.

findings.summary: The length-conversion formulas retained English unit names and decimal points.
evidence: The formulas used inch, foot, and decimal points inside a French presentation.
findings.resolution: Localized the unit names and standardized comma-decimal values.

findings.summary: The force conversion used lb, the mass symbol, instead of lbf.
evidence: The value 4,44822 N is a pound-force conversion and must use lbf.
findings.resolution: Changed the symbol to lbf.

findings.summary: The wire-gauge comparison table mistranslated BWG as GTB and mixed millimetre wording with symbols.
evidence: The header used GTB and the first row spelled out millimètres while later rows used mm.
findings.resolution: Restored BWG and consistent mm notation.

findings.summary: The gauge-number explanation used an unnecessary ordinary-number qualifier and jauge terminology.
evidence: The sentence said numéro de calibre ordinaire and la jauge 0.
findings.resolution: Rewrote it with calibre terminology and a direct higher-number rule.

findings.summary: The AWG formulas used decimal points in a comma-decimal French locale.
evidence: The constants were 0.005 and 0.127 while surrounding French values use commas.
findings.resolution: Changed them to 0,005 and 0,127.

findings.summary: The resistance paragraph used surface for conductor cross-section.
evidence: The context is the conductor's section transversale, not a surface in general.
findings.resolution: Rewrote it with section transversale and the square-of-diameter relationship.

findings.summary: The wire-system instruction used the literal verb Nommez.
evidence: The specification is an instruction to state or indicate the system.
findings.resolution: Changed it to Indiquez le système.
